This Mfa Is Filed U/S. 173(1) Of Mv Act Praying To
Set Aside The Judgement And Award Dated 11.06.2015
Passed By The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal At
Raichur In Mvc No.303/2014 And To Modify The
Compensation Awarded And To Pass Such Other
Orders As This Hon Ble Court Deems Fit Under The
Facts And Circumstances Of The Case.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Heard on admission.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his argument that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding driving license at the relevant point of time.
The Investigating officer has submitted charge sheet for the commission of offences punishable under Section 181 R/w 3 of MV Act.
However, the tribunal has fasten the liability on the Insurance company, which is contrary to law.
On all these ground sought for allow this appeal.

3. I have carefully gone through the judgment of the tribunal in para Nos.14 and 15, the tribunal has observed as under:
"14)

Therefore, the Hon'ble High Court has held that only because the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against driver for the offence u/sec.3 r/w.sec. 181 of M.V. Act it is not sufficient to prove that driver had no valid and effective driving license.
When the insurance company has taken specific plea, the burden is on the Insurance company to prove the said contention otherwise the plea remains as plea only without proof.
In the above referred other cases also, similar observations are made by the Hon'ble High Court.

Ultimately the Hon'ble High Court has dismissed The Manager vs Mukamma Mukamma W/O Husainappa on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142838499/

sentences.text: the above stated appeal filed by the insurance company and fastening of the liability on the insurance company was affirmed.
Similarly, in another decision in MFA.No.30390/2011 (MV) decided on 25.06.2013 our Hon'ble High Court has followed the same principle as stated above.
It has been held in the said case that when the insurance company has pleaded that driver of the offending vehicle had no driving license, it is for the insurance company to prove the same.
It is clearly held that onus is on the insurance company to prove that driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
Mere production of charge sheet filed by the police against the driver for the offence u/sec.3 r/w.sec.181 of M.V. Act is not sufficient to prove the said contention.
Similar observations are made by the Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.32703/2011 decided on 08.04.2014.
In that case our Hon'ble High Court has held that "Mere filing of a charge sheet is a matter of accusation against the driver that he was not holding a license.
But to prove that the driver had no license on the date of the accident, it would be determined by the court only after recording the evidence and rendering a judgment in a criminal case.
No copy of the judgment made available.

Therefore, mere fact that there is charge-sheet against the driver, for not holding a license and contravention of section 3 r/w.sec.181 of M.V. Act itself is sufficient to hold that the driver was not holding a license."
In the present case also respondent No.3 has not produced any judgment of the criminal court holding respondent No. I guilty of the offence u/sec.3 r/w.sec. 181 of M.V. Act.

Under these circumstances,
in view of the above referred decisions and evidence on record I hold that respondent No.3 has miserably failed to prove his contention that respondent No.1 had no valid and effective driving license to drive the offending vehicle in question at the time of accident.
The question of permit and other documents does not arise, since it is a case of third party claim.
15) I have gone through the decisions relied on by the learned counsel for respondent No.3 reported in 2014 ACJ 523. 2007 (5) K.L.J 65 & 2004 ACJ 2094.

The first decision is in respect of claim petition decided by the Workman Compensation Commissioner in which liability of the insurance company was absolved for the reason that driver of the vehicle had no effective driving license.
Second and third decisions are rendered in respect of permit for the use of tractor & trailer together.
In the present case, these decisions will not help respondent No.3 as the petitioners claim is a third party claim.
Therefore, decisions relied on by learned counsel for respondent No.3 will not help him to prove issue No.2.

Under these circumstances I hold that respondent No.3 has failed to prove issue No.2 and as such respondent No.3 being insurer in respect of the offending vehicle, the policy being in force at the time of accident, is liable to indemnify the liability of the insured namely respondent No.2.

Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative and Issue No.2 in the negative."
4. The tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and fasten the liability on the insurance company.
Even if it presume that the driver of the vehicle was not having valid and effective license as on the date of accident.

The Insurance company cannot escape from its liability, in view of decision of Hon'ble Apex court reported in the case of Pappu & Ors vs.
Vinod Kumar Lamba & Another reported in AIR 2018 SC 592.

sentences.text: Viewed from any angle, that there are no grounds to interfere with the judgment and award passed by the tribunal.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1) The tribunal has not passed the order as to joint and several liability.
Hence, to some extent the modified is required.
Appeal is partly allowed.

2) The judgment and award passed by the tribunal is modified as under:
a. Respondent No.1 is being the driver, respondent No.2 is being owner and respondent No.3 is being the Insurance company are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
b. Respondent No.3-Insurance company is directed to deposit the amount and disburse the same to the claimant.
c. The respondent No.3-Insurance company is at liberty to recover the in accordance with law.
